sentences.text: Kunbarrasaurus was a small, quadrupedal, armoured dinosaur that lived in Australia during the Early Cretaceous.
Scientists estimate this creature measured between 2.5 and 3.5 meters in length.
Its body was protected by bony armour covering the head, back, abdomen, legs, and tail.
This diverse armour included small ossicles, keeled scutes on the body and neck, non-keeled scutes on the snout, spike-like scutes on the hips, and triangular plates on the tail.
A preserved ring of scutes was found encircling the neck.
The skull roof is almost perfectly flat, except for limited convexity in the postorbital and nasal bones.
Unlike many relatives, the supraorbital bone consists of a single piece rather than two or three.
The side of the braincase was largely cartilage, forcing many brain nerves to exit through a single large opening.
The inner ear was very large and unique among dinosaurs, featuring a vestibule not separated from the brain cavity, a non-bony cochlear floor, and shortened semicircular canals.
Remains of the animal's last meal were preserved in the belly region of the holotype specimen.
Direct evidence of diet exists in the form of gut contents found in the holotype, unlike most herbivorous dinosaurs.
The first skeleton was discovered in November 1989 at Marathon Station near Richmond, Queensland.
Kunbarrasaurus ieversi was formally named and described in 2015 by a team including Lucy G. Leahey and Ralph E. Molnar.
The genus name Kunbarrasaurus comes from the Mayi word 'Kunbarra', meaning 'shield'.
The holotype specimen QM F1801 was found in the Allaru Formation, dating to the late Albian or possibly early Cenomanian.
This specimen includes an almost complete skeleton with the skull, vertebral column up to the middle tail, shoulder girdle, arm, pelvis, thighbones, and most of the body armour.
Kunbarrasaurus was a herbivore, like other ankylosaurians.
Clean cuts on plant fragments and the absence of stomach stones suggest the animal used oral processing to grind food.
In 2021, analysis placed Kunbarrasaurus in the basal Southern Hemisphere lineage Parankylosauria.
Phylogenetic analyses suggest Kunbarrasaurus is the sister taxon to the clade containing Stegouros and Antarctopelta.
Kunbarrasaurus lived between 106.3 and 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage.
It is debated whether a 2022 specimen from Warra Station belongs to Kunbarrasaurus leversi, as its authors noted it lacked unique features shared with the type specimen.
